§ 2Content

§ 3INDUS VALLEY CIVILIZATION

Drainage System

  • Most distinctive feature of Harappa Civilization.
  • Grid pattern roads / streets, intersecting at right angle. E.g. Lothal.

Domestic Architecture

  • The IVC was known for its advanced urban planning and well-structured houses.
  • The houses were made of burnt bricks (baked bricks).
  • Doors were made of wood.
  • Every house had its own bathroom.
  • Sump or Cesspit were made between drains to clean and trap solid waste.
  • Limestone slabs were used as drain covers.
  • Many houses had their own private wells.
  • Six granaries in each row (two rows)
  • Total: 12 granaries
  • Found in: Harappa
  • Roads cut each other at 90°

Tracking Social Differences

Studying Burials

  • Some of the graves contain pottery and ornaments as belief that it can be used in afterlife.
  • Jewelleries were found in burial of both men and women.
  • Dead were buried with copper mirrors.
  • Burial of dogs along with their masters.

Note

  • Ornaments, consisting of three shell rings, a Jasper Bead and hundred of micro beads, was found near the skull of a male at Harappa.

Craft Production

  • Chanhudaro: Devoted to craft production including bead making, shell cutting, metal working, seal making, and weight making.
  • Nageshwar (Gujarat) and Balakot (Pakistan): They were centres for shell making (Bangles, Ladles, and Inlay).

Trade & Commerce

  • Nageshwar and Balakot: Shell
  • Shortugai: Lapis Lazuli
  • South Rajasthan & North Gujarat: Carnelian
  • Khetri and Oman: Steatite (soft stone)
  • South India: Copper and Gold
  • Kolar (Karnataka): Gold

Map 2: Mesopotamia Civilisation around Tigris and Euphrates river (showing Egypt, Jericho, Catalhoyuk, Fertile Crescent, Mesopotamia, Persian Gulf, Red Sea, Dead Sea, Mediterranean Sea, Dilmun, Magan)

Harappan Seals

  • Harappan seals were made of steatite (a kind of soft stone).
  • Seals often contained animal motifs and a pictographic script.
  • The seals usually have a line of writing probably containing the name and title of the owner.

The Harappans were not aware about lion

§ 4INDUS VALLEY CIVILIZATION

Scripts

  • The scripts are not in alphabetical order and are pictographic.
  • Most inscriptions are short and the longest script contains about 26 signs.
  • They are written from right to left (script was known as: Boustrophedon).
  • They were found on jewellery, bone rods, seals, copper tools, jars, and an ancient signboard.
  • The scripts are undeciphered till date.

Weights

  • Barter system was prominent in IVC.
  • Exchange was regulated by a precise system of weights, usually made of a stone called "Chert".
  • Sukkur and Rohri hills: Limestone and Chert blades were mass produced and sent to various Harappan settlements in Sindh.
  • Lower denomination of weights: Binary
  • Higher denomination of weights: Decimal

IVC people did not know about iron.

Religious Practices

  • They worshipped unusual or unfamiliar objects such as Mother Goddess, Priest King, etc.
  • Fire altars were found at Kalibangan and Lothal.
  • The weights were uniform
  • Found in: Mohenjodaro
  • Height: 17.5 cm (6.9 inch)
  • Height: 10.5 cm

Religious Practices

Examining Seals

  • Unicorn: One Horned Animal.
  • Lingas: Conical stone objects worshipped as symbol of Shiva.
  • Proto Shiva seal (Pashupati).

Pottery Used

  • Ochre coloured pottery.
  • Black-Red ware pottery.
  • Painted-Grey ware pottery.

Possible Reasons for Decline of Harappa Civilization

  • Climate Change
  • Deforestation
  • Excessive Floods
  • Shifting or Drying up of Rivers
  • Foreign invasion

§ 6VEDIC AGE

Vedic Age (1500-600 BC)

  • Early Vedic Age (1500-1000 BC) → They were pastoral community
  • Later Vedic Age (1000-600 BC)
  • Bogazkoi inscription (Turkey): It mentioned names such as Indra, Varun, etc.

Note:

  • It is believed that Aryans arrived from Central Asia, where one group migrated from Turkey towards Europe and other came towards India.
  • Language of Aryans: Sanskrit
  • Aryans are considered to have codified the Vedas.

Similar sounding words

WordMeaning
BrahtaBrother
SaptaSeven
AndarUnder

VEDAS

  • There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda.
  • Oldest Text: Compiled during Zend-Avesta (Iran).
  • Meaning: Knowledge.
  • They were orally passed (Shruti) from one generation to another.
  • Apaurusheya: It is not created by man but gifted by God.

Bal Gangadhar Tilak

  • He compiled the book: The Arctic Home in the Vedas (he said "all Indians were Aryans").

Subdivisions of Vedas

SamhitaBrahmanasAranyakasUpanishads
Collection of Hymns (Sukta)Sacrifices and RitualsHermits (those who lived in jungles)Bhakti (talks about Bhakti Marga)

Rig Veda

  • It was the first Veda to be compiled.
  • It is made up of 10 mandalas.
  • It has the oldest and largest collection of Sanskrit hymns.
  • Total: 1028 hymns
  • Verses: 10,600
  • Hymns recited by Hotri.
  • Deities: Indra, Agni, Vishnu, and Varuna.
  • Female deities: Aditi, Usha (goddess of dawn).
  • Gayatri Mantra was written by Sage Vishwamitra for Goddess Savitri (mentioned in 3rd mandala).
  • Mandala no. 2-7 were created first.
  • 10th mandala mentions Purusha Sukta (considered a cosmic being).

Note: Upanishads are also known as "Vedanta" (end of Vedas).

Total: 108 Upanishads (Traditional)

Purusha Sukta

  • Mouth: Brahmans
  • Arms: Kshatriya
  • Thighs: Vaishya
  • Feet: Shudra

These four varnas are believed to have emerged from different parts of Purusha.

  • 9th mandala mentions: Lord Soma (Lord of Plants).
  • Somras is an energy drink.

Sama Veda

  • It is the oldest book on music.
  • It consists of chanting melodies.
  • It is composed of two Upanishads → Chandogya and Kena

Yajur Veda

  • It is the collection of mantras (rituals and sacrifices).
  • It is divided into two section → Shukla (meaning: White; contains Sathapatha Brahmana) and Krishna (meaning: Black).

Jabala Upanishad is a part of Yajur Veda.

Important Upanishads

  • Brihadaranyaka (oldest Upanishad).
  • Katha (contains story of Nachiketa and Yama (God of Death)).

Atharva Veda

  • Veda of magic formulas to ward off evil spirits and diseases (black magic).
  • It is divided into 20 khandas.

Important Upanishads of Atharva Veda

  • Mundaka Upanishad: Satyameva Jayate taken from here.
  • Maha Upanishad: Vasudhaiva Kutumbhkam (meaning: "the whole world is one family") taken from Chapter 6 of Maha Upanishad.
  • Mandukya Upanishad.
